        "Parent read all 1728 lines of the exact five-path owned diff, including every new browser-test line and every removed xpcshell-test line. Production query creation moves into MessageListTracker. Browser5 registers the new browser file, while xpcshell retains its standard pagination task under a new name and removes five implementation-specific scenarios. No protocol equivalence or native/UI execution is inferred.",
        "The query now arms a timer before awaiting the next search-criteria check, only if autoPaginationTimeout is positive and the current page is nonempty. Delay uses the remaining budget measured from that page first-message time. The timer can complete the existing page while a pending asynchronous search remains unresolved. Normal continuation clears the scheduled timer and waits for an already-triggered addPage promise. Rejection/cancellation cleanup and event-loop scheduling limits are bounded gaps, not a claimed cure.",
        "MessageList.addPage captures the previous page, ignores empty/done cases, optionally awaits a page-approval callback under Cu.isInAutomation, appends a new page and resolves the previous page. Its existing 25 ms allowPagesToResolve yield is distinct from the pagination deadline. MessagePage records first-message time and exposes its deferred messages promise; list continuation derives whether an unread page remains, not merely isDone.",
        "The shared tracker stores approval and criteria hooks, passes the current hook into each newly created list/query, and the list/query retain that captured function. Resetting tracker hooks alone does not replace callbacks in already existing objects. MessageQuery still assigns its actual criteria method as the default; only a truthy override under Cu.isInAutomation replaces it, matching the author rebuttal to the reviewer suggestion to use null.",
        "New timeout tests hold message checks 3, 7, 12 and 31 on explicit deferred promises. They directly assert page sizes 2, 4, 5, 19 and 69 and minimum elapsed durations for default 1000 ms and explicit 1500 ms cases. Two early-return tests hold page completion and then abort, checking two pages. Disabled-timeout and immediate-ID tests use deliberate synchronous busy waits, not condition/event waits; do not generalize those simulations as preferred async waiting practice.",
        "The immediate-ID fixture starts msgCounter at 1 but increments it before searchResults.has(msgCounter), whose keys are 6 and 55. Those keys therefore select the fifth and fifty-fourth callback positions, rather than the sixth and fifty-fifth described by the setup. Its assertions check two returned messages, list ID shape and elapsed duration without checking the identities. The mismatch remains in the accepted test; no real message-order, test failure or runtime duplication is claimed.",
        "All new/changed assertion calls were manually read. Messages are nonempty and state expected results with should. The new file labels itself unit test although it is a browser harness file; terse and misspelled comments are scoped observations, not naming rules. Accepted later code switches these operations to pushPrefEnv/popPrefEnv; this is a later phase, not an original cleanup guarantee.",
